mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a month indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over two months signals increased consumer confidence and economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a strong labor market and increased consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month, combined with an increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5%, signals reduced consumer purchasing power and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases > 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods with sustained FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the quarters with GDP increase.
